doc.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

chapter: Making a living: studio and odd work
title: The only non-music job: draftsman at Hughes Aircraft
summary: Around 1957, newly married, he spent six months as a draftsman at Hughes Aircraft; otherwise he has worked in music, including shows and strip joints.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Has there been a time in your career where you’ve been tempted — either because financially or just because you were looking for something different where you got into non-musical jobs?

Only in the beginning. About 1957 it would have been when I was first married, I worked for about six months at an aircraft plant at Hughes Aircraft in Los Angeles, as a draftsman and industrial artist, which that isn’t even done anymore, it’s all graphic art now. We used to actually use pencils and sit at drafting boards if you could believe that.

And T-squares. But that was for about six months and other than that I have — well I have been just in the music business. Not always just jazz, I’ve done a lot of different kinds of work. You really have to to survive if you’re not going to teach or have some other means of support. So I’ve done a lot of show work and strip joints and everything.
